x: On May 2nd a few of our athletes were engaged at the Leyton Flood Light meeting and it was pleasing to have Ivan Mayers running so well over the 100 yards in really first class company to finish 4th in 10.1secs.

Of the events, five were on the field and the contribution of our boys in this section was 27 points to our grand total. Outstanding recollections of the meeting were a fine sprint double by Ivan Mayers, some grand half miling by J.
Ivan Mayers was also in the team and was placed 3rd in the 100 yards and was a member of the winning Relay team. At the Universities Athletic Championships held at Manchester on 26th May, J.P.
Most notable were the brilliant doubles of Brian Morris (Sussex 220 & 440 yds.), Ivan Mayers (Middlesex 100 & 220 yds.) and Clive Ryan (Surrey Junior 100 & 220 yds.).
The Field Events Section however, were conspicuous by their absence, as will be seen by the fact that Ivan Mayers won the Shot Put in addition to completing the double in the sprints.
Ivan Mayers equalled his own 9.9s. 100 yards record at the Kinnaird meeting. I should be interested to learn Mal Ash's heat time in the Kinnaird, or in the final if his time was taken.

In the Hop Step & Jump, a keen battle ensued between Norman Caves, Charlie Jones and Ivan Mayers. Norman eventually won with a 44'9" effort, but one wonders just how far Ivan would have got had he not repeatedly taken off well before the board - a very interesting contest to watch.
The shot brought out former sprinter Ivan Mayers, still talking of another short season, who was second; the winner being Dave Butler.
The teams of 1954, which included such athletes as Ivan Mayers and Clay Gibbs, have long since retired - excepting Ron of course, who is still most active.
Maurice O'Dell - 100 yds Championship 1925 - 1931 inclusive. 6. 1954 - team: Dennis Merrett,Ron Holtum,Basil Waldon,Ivan Mayers.

Belgrave's only win in the A.A.A. senior sprint relay championship came in 1954 when on July 31st at Birmingham the team of Dennis Merrett, Ron Holtum, Basil Walden and Ivan Mayers won their 4 x 110yds heat in 42.9 and then went on to take the final with the second best time recorded by a club team - 42.6.
The West Indies gave us a great sprinter in Ivan Mayers who anchored our winning team in the A.A.A. 4 x 100 metres Relay Team in 1954, he too represented his country.

Denis Merrett sprang a surprise with an excellent double in both sprints, defeating Basil Walden and Ivan Mayers. The 440 went as expected to Alan Sexton in the good time of 50.6 in atrocious conditions with Jim Heathfield 2nd.
Bob Taylor equalled the Middlesex record held by the great Arthur Wint in the 880 yards, and Ivan Mayers beat Ron Holtum in the sprints while Jack Brown won the Kent one mile.
